_note: Kindergarten "Short Vowels and CVC Words" (English literacy year, Part 12.3; types/_shared/cvc-k.js). `words`: the regular consonant-vowel-consonant words a kindergartner knows, by their short vowel (no blend, no digraph, no silent letter, no vowel that is not the short sound in General American: no put, son, was, has, his; no name, no word a parent would object to; words few kindergartners know or use, yam, ram, tan, cab, rod, peg, sub, cot, hog, fog, gas, left out after the teacher's review). Every printed word, every word of a chain and every second word of a pair comes from these lists; x words (box, fox, fix, mix) never stand in a chain (x is two sounds). `banned`: the never list, words that are never printed and never buildable in a gap (names, rude or unkind words). `noGap`: the words of the lists that make a word of the never list with one of the five vowels in their middle (h_g: hag; f_t: fat; r_n: ron): never a word with a gap for its vowel (written by bank.js, checked by the factory). `worked`: the grey example of the gaps of each vowel (no risky fill, never a before n or m). `noPrint`: words never printed (pet names any pictured animal: a cat is a pet). `animals`: the pictured animals. `pics`: the library picture of a word (colour themes only), each looked at. `write`: the pictures a kindergartner names with exactly that word (a word written under a picture, a word chosen for a picture); the others are print-only (they stand next to their printed word in a match, one at most on a page, or beside the top word of a ladder). `apart`: two pictures never on one page (a cap is a kind of hat; a cup, a mug and a jug all hold a drink).
